summary: Each counter call must return one value and can update its single captured integer in constant time, so the accepted closure matches the constant lower bound and has no genuine slower principal class for scaling.

optimality.argument: One invocation must produce one result, requiring Omega(1) work regardless of the total call count k. The accepted closure reads, returns, and increments one captured number with a fixed amount of work, giving O(1) time per call.

replacement_checks.evidence: Every invocation must perform at least constant work to return its required numeric result.
Post-increment returns and updates one captured integer using a fixed number of operations on every call.
Cases cover zero and one call, negative and positive starts, crossing zero, both starting bounds, and persistent state over a longer sequence.
